controls.name: C_scanner_finds_variables
controls.must_fire_because: the variable scanner must be able to see a variable at all; a regex that matched nothing would report a perfectly ground corpus and be indistinguishable from the claim being true
controls.can_fail_because: if VAR did not match MeTTa syntax, or the blobs were unreadable, source_var_count would be 0 everywhere and the scan would prove nothing
controls.null_must_contain: a corpus whose sources mention no variables, against which the scanner cannot be exercised
controls.detail: the scanner is exercised against real MeTTa source

controls.name: C_sources_resolve
controls.must_fire_because: every program must be matched to its shard blob by CID, or the source half of this measurement is about a subset nobody named
controls.can_fail_because: the CIDs in result.json could name blobs this store does not hold, e.g. a run against a store that has since been pruned
controls.null_must_contain: a store missing the shards, giving no sources
controls.detail: CID to blob resolution over the committed store

controls.name: C_execution_split_reproduces
controls.must_fire_because: the executed/not-executed split must reproduce CORPUS_COMPOSITION 's independently published 26 of 64, or this file's own notion of "executed" is a second, unvalidated instrument
controls.can_fail_because: keying "executed" off the resolver error string could miscount the 4 error-only programs, which DID execute and whose result is an assertion Error
controls.null_must_contain: a split that disagrees with the published one

falsifiers.name: F_corpus_not_all_ground
falsifiers.can_fail_because: any program that actually executed MeTTa recorded a result containing a variable token
falsifiers.null_must_contain: a corpus in which some executed program does produce a non-ground result
falsifiers.detail: variables surviving into a recorded result
falsifiers.refutes: the sentence "process reuse is safe for ground-result jobs, WHICH IS THE ENTIRE CORPUS" -- and with it M1.3b's closure of M1.1's largest open issue
falsifiers.fires_when: any program that actually executed MeTTa recorded a result containing a variable token
falsifiers.verdict: survived — the falsifier did not fire

falsifier: any executed program records a result containing a variable
